scenarios.notes: No dominant move found in 12 months, but I could not find any path to the 115 bonus: score drifts 100 to 87 and 'heading to 86'. Reassure calls give the same stock reply every time.

suggestions.what: Make every header meter tappable with the same why-list the Score popup has, including stability and legitimacy
suggestions.goal_served: Can find out why every number moved

suggestions.what: Show a path to the 115 score bonus (what raises security at war) or lower the bar for a Tough seat
suggestions.goal_served: No fake depth, tough nation with understandable limits

suggestions.what: Vary call replies by country and by relation, and show the relation numbers inside the call card
Show a number for every free order in the debrief (Mass troops)
Warn before political capital caps out, and let me bank by spending half
Let staff stop recommending a move that cannot help (Court Poland at -99)
suggestions.goal_served: AI that plays fair, advice that makes sense

delight: Forecast on the order menu says '73% chance', relations -30, and warns that the strike costs the Make peace bonus star (018-fc.png)
Score popup with base plus named terms (032-sc.png)
Debrief shows 70 to 90 mobilization with the stability cost and why numbers moved (013-mob.png)
Seed code dropped me into the exact Russia game

fun.reason: Real decisions and honest numbers, but months 4, 5, 11 felt like answering the same phone call.

clarity.reason: Previews, score breakdown, mission impact are strong; header meters unexplained and one broken layout.

visual.reason: Broadcast scenes look crafted; some art does not match the crisis and Full desk cards break.

feels_like_a_game.reason: Orders, forecasts, capital cap read as a game, though the same crisis types cycle.

agency.reason: Always saw why something was blocked or costly; the 115 bonus path and Poland advice left me guessing.

realism.reason: Gaza conference for Russia and boilerplate leader replies break it; leaders and war framing are right.

replay.reason: I would try Hunt spies and the ceasefire chain again, and a different seat; one repeated reply set limits it.

recommend.reason: Worth a strategy friend's evening, not yet a Paradox replacement; transparency is the selling point.

verbatim: The numbers are honest and I can usually see why, which is rare, but I want to tap Stability and get the same answer the Score gives me, and I do not want the same phone call three times.
